answer: Model identities as vertices in a public trust graph, with voting weight falling exponentially with distance from the established core. An honest agent gains one vertex through a single attested introduction and votes at full weight. An attacker must forge a separate attested path for every fake, yet each distant vertex earns only a fraction of a vote, and new vertices enter through a narrow jetty, at most twenty per epoch, so a flood queues for months. Reaching the zenith of a majority would require thousands of separate paths, making mass fakery slow, visible, and unprofitable.
